articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractors leaked AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub because apparently irony is the only constant in cybersecurity. The agency tasked with protecting America's digital infrastructure couldn't protect their own cloud credentials from public embarrassment.

articles.title: GitHub says internal repos exfiltrated after poisoned VS Code extension attack
articles.summary: Claude's sandbox had a real vulnerability that Anthropic quietly patched without disclosure, because why alert the security community when you can just pretend it never happened. Another AI company treating CVEs like optional homework.

articles.title: Microsoft shuts down illegal code-signing operation used by ransomware crims to mask their malware
articles.summary: London police demanded Big Tech hand over communications data 700,000 times last year, proving that mass surveillance is alive and well in the surveillance state formerly known as England. FOIA requests: the last bastion of accountability.

articles.title: Microsoft Open-Sources RAMPART and Clarity to Secure AI Agents During Development
articles.summary: America's top cyber defense agency left a GitHub repo open with files literally named 'AWS-Workspace-Firefox-Passwords.csv' because subtlety is apparently not taught at cybersecurity school. CISA proving that irony truly is dead.

articles.title: Show HN: Bypassing the AWS Lambda 4KB limit to run polyglot AI agents
articles.summary: GitHub got breached and 3,800+ internal repos were exfiltrated by TeamPCP, because even the platform that hosts everyone else's code can't keep their own secure. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a commit message.

articles.title: DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 showcased 47 unique zero-days worth $1.3 million in bounties, proving that responsible disclosure still pays better than the dark web. White hat hackers eating well while keeping enterprise software honest.

articles.title: Zscaler Partners with Global System Integrators to Launch Project AI-Guardian to Help Accelerate Enterprise AI Adoption
articles.summary: DirtyDecrypt PoC drops for Linux kernel CVE-2026-31635, another local privilege escalation bug with a catchy name. Because apparently every kernel vulnerability needs to sound like a rejected action movie title.

articles.title: Crook leaks 468k+ records, claims they pwned Portugal’s postal carrier
articles.summary: ShinyHunters is harassing cybersecurity firm Unit 221B for telling victims not to pay ransoms, proving that crime syndicates have thinner skin than teenage gamers. Extortionists mad that someone won't play their game.

articles.title: Grafana Labs refuses ransom after hackers steal already-open-source code
articles.summary: TeamPCP's supply chain campaign continues with confirmed Checkmarx Jenkins plugin compromise and a self-spreading worm across npm and PyPI. Software supply chains remain the gift that keeps on giving to threat actors.

articles.title: ABB CoreSense HM and CoreSense M10
articles.summary: Verizon DBIR 2026 reveals vulnerability exploitation is now the #1 attack vector while remediation gets slower, creating a perfect storm of incompetence. Attackers are getting faster while defenders are getting... creative with their excuses.
